facts.statement: The animal belongs to the genus Sauroposeidon.
facts.quote: genus: Sauroposeidon

facts.statement: The species name is proteles.
facts.quote: species: proteles

facts.statement: Superposeidon is a synonym of Sauroposeidon resulting from a clerical error.
facts.quote: synonyms: *Superposeidon Brochu, Long, McHenry, Scanlon, & Willis, 2002 (lapsus calami)

facts.statement: The fossils date from the Early Cretaceous, specifically between 113 and 110 million years ago.
facts.quote: The fossils were found in rocks dating from near the end of the Early Cretaceous (Aptian–early Albian), from about 113 to 110 million years ago

facts.statement: Paleoecological analysis indicates the animal lived on the shores of the Gulf of Mexico in a river delta.
facts.quote: Sauroposeidon lived on the shores of the Gulf of Mexico, in a river delta

facts.statement: The holotype remains were discovered in 1994 but were initially misidentified as petrified wood due to their size and age.
facts.quote: While the holotype remains were initially discovered in 1994, due to their unexpected age and unusual size they were initially misclassified as pieces of petrified wood

facts.statement: Estimates suggest the animal reached lengths of 27 to 34 meters and masses of 40 to 60 metric tons.
facts.quote: With an estimated length of 27 - 34 m and a mass of 40 - 60 MT, it also ranks among the longest and heaviest

facts.statement: Extrapolations suggest the animal's head could reach a height of 16.5 to 18 meters, making it one of the tallest known dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Extrapolations based on the more completely known Brachiosaurus indicate that the head of Sauroposeidon could reach 16.5 – 18 m in height with its neck extended, which would make it one of the tallest known dinosaurs

facts.statement: The first fossils were four neck vertebrae found in rural Oklahoma dating to about 110 million years ago.
facts.quote: The first fossils classified as Sauroposeidon were four neck vertebrae discovered in rural Oklahoma, not far from the Texas border, in a claystone outcrop that dates the fossils to about 110 million years ago (mya)

facts.statement: The vertebrae were discovered in May 1994 at the Antlers Formation in Atoka County, Oklahoma, by dog trainer Bobby Cross.
facts.quote: These vertebrae were discovered in May 1994 at the Antlers Formation in Atoka County, Oklahoma by dog trainer Bobby Cross

facts.statement: A press release was issued in October 1999, followed by publication in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology in March 2000.
facts.quote: Upon their realization of the find's significance, they issued a press release in October 1999, followed by official publication of their findings in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology in March 2000

facts.statement: The species was named S. proteles, with the holotype specimen designated OMNH 53062.
facts.quote: The new species was named S. proteles, and the holotype is OMNH 53062

facts.statement: In 2012, numerous sauropod remains previously known under different names were reclassified into the genus Sauroposeidon.
facts.quote: In 2012, numerous other sauropod remains that had been known for decades under various different names were also classified in the genus Sauroposeidon

facts.statement: In 2012, re-analysis led paleontologists to conclude that Paluxysaurus was the same animal as Sauroposeidon and a junior synonym of S. proteles.
facts.quote: In 2012, re-analysis of these specimens in light of additional Sauroposeidon remains led paleontologists D'Emic and Foreman to conclude that Paluxysaurus was the same animal as Sauroposeidon, and thus a junior synonym of S. proteles

facts.statement: Students from the University of Texas at Austin discovered a bonebed in Hood County in the mid-1980s, but work stopped in 1987.
facts.quote: In the mid-1980s, students from the University of Texas at Austin discovered a bonebed on a ranch in Hood County, but early work stopped in 1987

facts.statement: The quarry was reopened in 1993 and worked by teams from Southern Methodist University, the Fort Worth Museum of Science and History, and Tarleton State University.
facts.quote: The quarry was reopened in 1993 and was subsequently worked by parties from Southern Methodist University, the Fort Worth Museum of Science and History, and Tarleton State University

facts.statement: The name Paluxysaurus was based on a partial skull including a left maxilla, nasal, and teeth.
facts.quote: The name Paluxysaurus was based on the specimen FWMSH 93B-10-18, a partial skull including an associated left maxilla, nasal, and teeth

facts.statement: It is debated whether the animal is closely related to Brachiosaurus, which could make size estimates inaccurate.
facts.quote: However, this animal may not be as closely related to Brachiosaurus as previously thought, so these estimates may be inaccurate

facts.statement: There are differences between some specimens, but they cannot be confidently distinguished from each other.
facts.quote: There are differences in the remains of P. sp. and Paluxysaurus, but they cannot be distinguished with confidence

facts.statement: The original fossil find consisted of four connected mid-neck vertebrae along with their attached ribs.
facts.quote: The original Sauroposeidon find was composed of four articulated, mid-cervical vertebrae (numbers 5 to 8), with the cervical ribs in place.

facts.statement: Its largest neck vertebra measures 1.4 meters in length, which is the longest sauropod neck vertebra ever recorded.
facts.quote: The vertebrae are extremely elongated, with the largest one having an overall length of 1.4 m, making it the longest sauropod neck vertebra on record.

facts.statement: The neck bones were extremely thin and filled with tiny air cells, similar to chicken or ostrich bones, to reduce weight.
facts.quote: Examination of the bones revealed that they are honeycombed with tiny air cells, and are very thin, like the bones of a chicken or an ostrich, making the neck lighter and easier to lift.

facts.statement: Its longest measurable neck rib is 3.42 meters long, which is 18% longer than the longest rib of Giraffatitan.
facts.quote: The cervical ribs were remarkably long as well, with the longest measurable rib (on vertebra 6) measuring 3.42 m – about 18% longer than the longest rib reported for Giraffatitan, but exceeded in length by the cervical ribs of Mamenchisaurus.

facts.statement: It could likely raise its head between 16.5 and 18 meters above the ground, reaching the height of a six-story building.
facts.quote: Sauroposeidon was probably able to raise its head 16.5 – 18 m above the ground, which is as high as a six-story building.

facts.statement: Scientists estimate its shoulder height was between 6 and 7 meters based on comparisons to brachiosaurids.
facts.quote: Sauroposeidon's shoulder height has been estimated at 6 - 7 m based on an interpretation of the animal as a brachiosaurid.

facts.statement: Estimates of its total body length range from 27 to 34 meters.
facts.quote: Estimates of its total possible length have ranged from 27 m to 34 m.

facts.statement: Its estimated mass ranges from 40 to 60 metric tons.
facts.quote: The mass of Sauroposeidon is estimated at 40 - 60 MT.

facts.statement: Researchers debate whether the mass estimate is too high, suggesting the rest of its body might have been as slender as its neck.
facts.quote: However, Sauroposeidon has a gracile neck compared to Giraffatitan. If the rest of the body turns out to be similarly slender, the mass estimate may be too high.

facts.statement: It is debated whether sauropods possessed an air sac system that could reduce mass estimates by 20% or more.
facts.quote: In addition, it is possible that sauropods may have had an air sac system, like those in birds, which could reduce all sauropod mass estimates by 20% or more.

facts.statement: It lived on the shores of the ancient Gulf of Mexico in a vast river delta environment similar to the modern Mississippi delta.
facts.quote: Sauroposeidon lived on the shores of the Gulf of Mexico, which ran through Oklahoma at that time, in a vast river delta similar to the Mississippi delta today.

facts.statement: Juveniles were likely preyed upon by apex predators such as Acrocanthosaurus atokensis and Deinonychus antirrhopus, while adults had few natural predators.
facts.quote: There were few predators which could attempt to attack a full-grown Sauroposeidon, but juveniles were likely to be preyed on by the contemporary Acrocanthosaurus atokensis (a carnosaur slightly smaller than a Tyrannosaurus), which likely were the apex predators in this region, and the small dromaeosaur Deinonychus antirrhopus.

facts.statement: Scientists estimate it lived approximately 110 million years ago during the Aptian and Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: Scientists have used biostratigraphic data and the fact that it shares several of the same genera as the Trinity Group of Texas, to surmise that this formation was laid down during the Aptian and Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous Period, approximately 110 mya.

facts.statement: The genus Sauroposeidon was named by Wedel et al. in 2000.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Wedel et al., 2000

facts.statement: The species S. proteles was named by Wedel et al. in 2000.
facts.quote: species_authority: Wedel et al., 2000

facts.statement: It has been synonymized with Superposeidon and Paluxysaurus jonesi, though these names are considered invalid or lapsus calami.
facts.quote: synonyms: *Superposeidon Brochu, Long, McHenry, Scanlon, & Willis, 2002 (lapsus calami) Paluxysaurus jonesi Rose, 2007

facts.statement: It is known from incomplete specimens, including a bone bed and fossilized tracks found in Oklahoma, Wyoming, and Texas.
facts.quote: Conocido solo por varios ejemplares incompletos, incluyendo un lecho de huesos y rastros fosilizados que se han encontrado en los estados norteamericanos de Oklahoma, Wyoming y Texas.

facts.statement: It is known as the last North American sauropod before a 40-million-year gap in the continent's record, which ended with the appearance of Alamosaurus.
facts.quote: Es conocido como el último saurópodo de América del Norte, antes de una ausencia del grupo en el continente que duró 40 millones de años, que terminó con la aparición de Alamosaurus durante el Maastrichtiense.

facts.statement: When discovered in 1994, the remains were mistakenly identified as petrified wood.
facts.quote: Cuando fueron hallados, en 1994, los restos se identificaron erróneamente como madera petrificada.

facts.statement: A detailed analysis in 1999 revealed their true nature, leading to media attention and a formal publication in 2000.
facts.quote: Un análisis más detallado de 1999 reveló su verdadera naturaleza, dando lugar a un cierto revuelo en los medios de comunicación, y a la publicación formal, que apareció un año después (Wedel et al., 2000).

facts.statement: Sauroposeidon could reach a height of 13.5 meters, making it one of the tallest dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Las estimaciones indican que Sauroposeidon podría alcanzar 13,5 metros de altura, con un cuello ancho, haciéndole uno de los dinosaurios más altos.

facts.statement: Sauroposeidon likely had shoulders reaching a height of 5 meters.
facts.quote: Los hombros llegaban probablemente a los 5 metros de altura.

facts.statement: Sauroposeidon had an estimated length of up to 27 meters and a mass between 36 and 40 tonnes.
facts.quote: Con una longitud estimada de hasta 27 metros y una masa de entre 36 a 40 toneladas.

facts.statement: Until 2006, Sauroposeidon was likely the tallest dinosaur ever unearthed, though it was neither the longest nor the heaviest.
facts.quote: Mientras que es verdad que Sauroposeidon sea probablemente el dinosaurio más alto exhumado hasta 2006, no es ni el más largo ni el más masivo.

facts.statement: The original Sauroposeidon specimen consisted of four articulated middle cervical vertebrae, numbers 5 to 8, with cervical ribs in place.
facts.quote: El hallazgo original de Sauroposeidon estaba compuesto por cuatro vértebras cervicales medias articuladas, números 5 a 8, con las costillas cervicales en su lugar.

facts.statement: The largest cervical vertebra of Sauroposeidon measured 1.4 meters in total length, making it the longest sauropod neck vertebra on record.
facts.quote: Las vértebras son extremadamente alargadas, y la más grande tiene una longitud total de 1,4 metros, lo que la convierte en la vértebra del cuello de saurópodo más larga registrada.

facts.statement: Sauroposeidon could likely raise its head 17 to 18 meters above the ground, equivalent to a six-story building.
facts.quote: Sauroposeidon probablemente podría levantar su cabeza 17-18 metros sobre el suelo, que es tan alto como un edificio de seis pisos.

facts.statement: Estimates for Sauroposeidon's total possible length have ranged between 27 and 34 meters.
facts.quote: Las estimaciones de su longitud total posible han oscilado entre 27 metros y 34 metros.

facts.statement: The estimated mass of Sauroposeidon ranges from 40 to 60 tonnes.
facts.quote: La masa de Sauroposeidon se estima en 40-60 toneladas.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Sauroposeidon is as closely related to Brachiosaurus as previously thought, which could make size estimates inaccurate.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, este animal puede no estar tan relacionado con Brachiosaurus como se pensaba anteriormente, por lo que estas estimaciones pueden ser inexactas.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that if the rest of Sauroposeidon's body was equally slender, the mass estimate might be too high.
facts.quote: Si el resto del cuerpo resulta ser igualmente delgado, la estimación de masa puede ser demasiado alta.

facts.statement: Sauroposeidon was discovered in 1994 in the Antlers Formation by Dr. Richard Cifelli and his team from the Oklahoma Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: Los restos fueron descubiertos en 1994 en la Formación Antlers por el Dr. Richard Cifelli y su equipo del Museo de Historia Natural de Oklahoma.

facts.statement: The first specimen consisted of four neck vertebrae found in rural Atoka County, Oklahoma, in rock exposures dating to approximately 110 million years ago, specifically between the Aptian and Albian stages.
facts.quote: El primer espécimen hallado está representado por cuatro vértebras del cuello, descubiertas en la Oklahoma rural, en el condado de Atoka, no lejos de la frontera con Texas, en un afloramiento rocoso de cerca de 110 millones de años, específicamente entre el Aptiense y el Albiense.

facts.statement: The initial remains were mistakenly identified as petrified wood.
facts.quote: Inicialmente se identificaron erróneamente como madera petrificada.

facts.statement: Three years after discovery, Dr. Cifelli assigned the remains to graduate student Matt Wedel for analysis, leading to a re-evaluation of the specimen.
facts.quote: No fue sino hasta tres años más tarde, cuando el Dr. Cifelli las asignó a un estudiante graduado, Matt Wedel, para que las analizara como parte de un proyecto, que el espécimen fue nuevamente estudiado.

facts.statement: A press conference was held in October 1999, followed by the official publication in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology in March 2000.
facts.quote: Los resultados de este análisis revelaron la significancia del hallazgo, por lo que se realizó una conferencia de prensa en octubre de 1999, seguida por la publicación oficial en el Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology en marzo de 2000.

facts.statement: The new species was named S. proteles, with the holotype designated as OMNH 53062.
facts.quote: La nueva especie fue llamada S. proteles y su holotipo es OMNH 53062.

facts.statement: Immediate media attention led some sources to incorrectly label it as the largest dinosaur in history.
facts.quote: Atrajo la atención de los medios de comunicación de inmediato, lo que llevó a algunas fuentes a llamarlo incorrectamente como el dinosaurio más grande de la historia.

facts.statement: Additional finds in the Cloverly Formation, Wyoming, suggested Sauroposeidon belongs to the clade Somphospondyli rather than the family Brachiosauridae, as initially thought in 1999.
facts.quote: Descubrimientos adicionales de otros restos hallados en la Formación Cloverly, en Wyoming, sugirieron que Sauroposeidon pertenece al clado Somphospondyli, en lugar de incluirse en Brachiosauridae, como se pensó cuando fue identificado en 1999.

facts.statement: In 2012, many other saurpod remains known for decades under various names were also classified into the genus Sauroposeidon.
facts.quote: En 2012, muchos otros restos de saurópodos que se conocían durante décadas con varios nombres diferentes también se clasificaron en el género Sauroposeidon.

facts.statement: In 2012, paleontologists D'Emic and Foreman concluded that Paluxysaurus was the same animal as Sauroposeidon, making it a junior synonym of S. proteles.
facts.quote: En 2012, el nuevo análisis de estos especímenes a la luz de restos adicionales de Sauroposeidon llevó a los paleontólogos D'Emic y Foreman a concluir que Paluxysaurus era el mismo animal que Sauroposeidon y por lo tanto un sinónimo más moderno de S. proteles.

facts.statement: The genus name Sauroposeidon comes from Greek words meaning "lizard" and "Poseidon," referencing the idea that the dinosaur's weight caused the ground to tremble as it walked.
facts.quote: El nombre del género proviene del griego sauros, σαύρος, para "lagarto" y Poseidón, 'Ποσειδών, el dios del mar y los terremotos de la mitología griega, Esta es una referencia a la noción de que el peso de un saurópodo era tan grande que el suelo temblaba mientras caminaba.

facts.statement: The species name proteles means "perfect before the end" in Greek, indicating it was one of the last and most specialized giant sauropods of North America.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, proteles, πρωτέλης, también proviene del griego, y significa "perfecto antes del final", señalándolo como uno de los últimos y más especializados saurópodos gigantes de Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Sauroposeidon was initially considered to be closely related to Brachiosaurus and Giraffatitan, both members of the family Brachiosauridae.
facts.quote: Sauroposeidon proteles fue considerado en un principio una especie con afinidades a Brachiosaurus y Giraffatitan, ambos incluidos en la familia Brachiosauridae.

facts.statement: Recent studies contradict this assumption, classifying Sauroposeidon as a basal member of the clade Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estudios recientes contradicen esta suposición señalando a Sauroposeidon como un miembro basal del clado Somphospondyli.

facts.statement: Sauroposeidon lived from the Aptian to the Cenomanian stages, approximately 121.4 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Cenomanian (121.4 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The discovery of Sauroposeidon consisted of four middle cervical vertebrae, numbers 5 to 8, with their associated cervical ribs in place.
facts.quote: El hallazgo de Sauroposeidon consistió en el descubrimiento de cuatro vértebras cervicales medias, números 5 a 8, con las costillas cervicales en su lugar.

facts.statement: The vertebrae are extremely elongated, with the largest measuring about 1.2 meters in length, the most elongated in the fossil record.
facts.quote: Las vértebras son extremadamente alargadas, con la mayor midiendo unos 1,2 metros de largo, las más alargadas en el registro fósil.

facts.statement: The bones were alveolated with small air-filled cells and very thin, like chicken or ostrich bones, making the structure much lighter and easier to move; the longest cervical rib measured 3.42 meters, about 18% longer than the largest rib of Giraffatitan but shorter than those of Mamenchisaurus.
facts.quote: El examen de los huesos reveló que son alveolados con pequeñas celdas llenas de aire, y muy finos, como los huesos de pollo o avestruz, lo que hace al conjunto mucho más liviano y más fácil de mover, también las costillas cervicales eran largas y fuertes, de las cuales la mayor medida fue la correspondiente a la vértebra 6 midiendo 3,42 metros, alrededor de un 18% más larga que la mayor costilla de Giraffatitan, pero menores en largo a las de Mamenchisaurus.

facts.statement: While its vertebrae are 25–33% longer than those of Giraffatitan, they are only 10–15% larger in diameter.
facts.quote: Mientras que sus vértebras son un 25–33% más largas que las de Giraffatitan, son solamente 10–15% más grandes en diámetro.

facts.statement: The neck length is estimated at 11.25 to 12 meters, compared to the 9 meters possessed by the HM SII specimen of Giraffatitan.
facts.quote: La longitud del cuello se estima en 11,25 a 12 metros, en comparación a los 9 metros que posee el HM SII.

facts.statement: Giraffatitan is estimated to have weighed between 36 and 40 tons, based on an average obtained through various methodologies.
facts.quote: Se considera que Giraffatitan pudo haber pesado entre 36 a 40 toneladas. Esta estimación es un promedio obtenido mediante diversas metodologías.

facts.statement: However, the relatively gracile neck of Sauroposeidon suggests that if its body followed the same proportions, the previous weight estimate might be too high.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el cuello relativamente grácil de Sauroposeidon, da lugar a otra conjetura: si su cuerpo seguía la misma proporción, la estimación anterior podría ser demasiado elevada.

facts.statement: It is possible that sauropods had an air sac system like modern birds, which could reduce all mass estimates by 20% or more.
facts.quote: Finalmente, es posible que los saurópodos tuvieran un sistema de sacos de aire, como las aves modernas, lo que podría reducir todas las estimaciones sobre la masa en un 20% o más.
